title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
abstract: arXiv:2611.18272v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. The approach employs a general six-stage process with platform-specific adapters, utilizing either a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock to identify and read tensor allocations from video memory. We validate this acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, demonstrating that the recovered bytes are byte-exact and usable

translated_title: 从字节到行为：基于运行中GPU隐藏状态的请求级归因
translated_abstract: 现有的针对机器学习系统的内存取证通常面向静态产物，例如模型权重或提示词日志，而非运行中推理过程的瞬态计算状态。这一空白限制了取证分析人员对无法重启或修改的、正在运行的大语言模型（LLM）服务进行具体行为分析的能力。我们提出了一种方法，利用非修改式调试器从运行中的GPU进程获取逐层残差流激活值，且无需预先了解模型的架构参数或权重。该方法采用一个通用的六阶段流程并配合平台特定的适配器，通过PyTorch分配器时钟或内核启动时钟来识别并读取显存中的张量分配。我们在涵盖九种架构类别的33个开源仅解码器（decoder-only）模型上验证了该采集方法，证明恢复出的字节达到字节级精确且可用。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无需修改进程、无需预知模型架构或权重的取证方法，可直接从运行中的GPU进程提取逐层残差流激活值，实现对无法重启或修改的大语言模型服务的请求级行为归因分析。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a non-invasive forensic method that extracts per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process—without prior knowledge of the model's architecture or weights—enabling request-level attribution of running LLM services that cannot be restarted or modified.
